reports.title: Règlement sur le régime de péréquation (Regulation respecting the equalization scheme)
reports.description: Consolidated regulation (CQLR c. F-2.1, r. 11) under the Act respecting municipal taxation establishing Quebec's municipal equalization scheme. Standardized property wealth is established under s. 9 'conformément à la section I du chapitre XVIII.1 de la Loi' from the municipal property assessment roll, and population under s. 8 is 'la plus élevée entre celle relative à cet exercice et celle relative à l'un ou l'autre des 3 exercices précédant l'exercice de référence'. The regulation names no external statistical agency for its inputs, which is why this node is isolated: its inputs are municipal rolls and decree-based population figures, not published statistical releases.
reports.cadence_note: A consolidated regulation, reprinted on amendment rather than published on a schedule; allocations under it run annually.

entries.covers: Annual equalization payment deadline for the 2027 fiscal year

release_schedule.rule: Le ministre verse le montant de péréquation déterminé pour un exercice financier... au plus tard le 30 juin de l'exercice courant (Règlement sur le régime de péréquation, F-2.1, r. 11, art. 33)
release_schedule.note: The regulation text itself (F-2.1, r. 11) is a consolidated document on LégisQuébec that is reprinted on amendment, not published on a fixed schedule — this matches the existing cadence_note. However, the regime it establishes has a stated annual deadline: Article 33 requires the Minister to pay the equalization amount no later than June 30 of the current fiscal year. That deadline for fiscal year 2026 (June 30, 2026) has already passed relative to today (2026-08-11), so the next occurrence is June 30, 2027. Article 15 also sets a September 1 cutoff for municipal financial summaries to be counted, and municipalities must submit summaries by May 1.

reports.title: Règlement sur la répartition entre les municipalités du montant représentant la croissance d'une partie de la taxe de vente du Québec
reports.description: Consolidated regulation (CQLR c. M-22.1, r. 1.2) apportioning among municipalities the amount established under s. 21.26 of the Act respecting the Ministère des Affaires municipales, des Régions et de l'Occupation du territoire, representing the growth of a portion of Quebec sales tax (QST) revenue. Distribution runs through two components (90% / 10% from fiscal 2030 onward), and the second component apportions by an economic vitality index whose source the regulation names outright.
reports.cadence_note: A consolidated regulation, reprinted on amendment rather than published on a schedule; the apportionment it governs runs annually.

release_schedule.note: Confirmed via LegisQuebec consolidated text (adopted 31 Oct 2024, last amended 5 Dec 2025, current version effective 1 Apr 2026): this is a consolidated regulation reprinted whenever amended, with no stated periodicity for amendments and no publication calendar. The regulation's own text contains no deadline/versement provision for this document itself (searched for '31 mai', 'versement', 'paiement' — none found in the regulation). Note: the annual apportionment amounts it governs ARE announced via a separate government news release each November (e.g. Nov 13, 2024 and Nov 18, 2024 articles announcing 2025 amounts, with 'versement...au plus tard le 31 mai 2025'), but that November/May cadence belongs to the annual decree/announcement process, not to this regulation document, which remains genuinely irregular in its own reprint/amendment schedule. This confirms rather than contradicts the existing cadence_note.

reports.title: Indice de vitalité économique des territoires
reports.publisher: Institut de la statistique du Québec
reports.description: Composite index of the economic vitality of Quebec municipalities and regional county municipalities (MRCs), computed as a geometric mean of three normalized indicators: rate of workers, median total income of individuals, and average annual population growth over five years. Consumed by name in the QST-growth apportionment regulation, which takes 'la dernière liste publiée par l'Institut de la statistique du Québec' as of 1 September of the preceding fiscal year.
reports.cadence_note: Refreshed every two years (handoff said annual; the ISQ page states biennial, next update March 2027; most recent edition released 26 February 2025 covering 2022 data).

entries.covers: Next biennial edition of the Economic Vitality Index (municipalities and RCMs)

release_schedule.note: The publisher's landing page states the index has an update frequency of every 2 years and explicitly lists 'Next update: March 2027'. The most recent edition (2022 data) was published February 26, 2025 as the 'Édition 2025' bulletin, consistent with a ~2-year cadence.

reports.title: Homelessness Prevention Program — allocations and program guidelines
reports.publisher: Ontario Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing
reports.description: Ontario's consolidated provincial funding program supporting the province's 47 municipal service managers 'to provide affordable housing and support services for people at risk of or experiencing homelessness'. Service managers 'are required to complete an annual investment plan outlining how they plan to use their HPP allocations each year for ministry approval'. The post-2023 allocation model, documented by the Auditor General of Ontario's 2023 follow-up, weights four Census-derived socioeconomic indicators for half of the allocation calculation alongside Ontario Works and ODSP caseload data.
reports.cadence_note: Annual allocations and investment-plan cycle; the allocation model itself was rebuilt in 2023.

entries.covers: 2023-24 HPP allocation notification to service managers
2024-25 HPP allocation (ministry stated it 'will not be available until early 2024')
2026-27 HPP allocation (Kingston council approved its 2026-27 investment plan, based on the province's allocation, on 2026-07-09)
Projected 2027-28 HPP allocation notification, ahead of the April 1 Ontario fiscal year start

release_schedule.note: No published release calendar exists. HPP allocations are issued annually by the ministry to Consolidated Municipal Service Managers/DSSABs ahead of each Ontario fiscal year (April 1-March 31); service managers then submit an annual investment plan. Observed notification timing clusters in the first few months of the calendar year (e.g., 2023-24 allocation announced Feb 3, 2023; 2024-25 allocation described by the ministry as not available 'until early 2024'), consistent with the corpus's existing cadence_note describing an annual allocation/investment-plan cycle rebuilt in 2023. Exact month varies year to year and no fixed statutory date was found, so this is modeled as an observed pattern rather than a stated rule.

dependencies.basis: REMAPPED SOURCE. The handoff attached this edge to qc-perequation; the citing regulation is not the péréquation regulation but the QST-growth apportionment regulation, M-22.1, r. 1.2, whose s. 3(2°) defines the economic vitality index of a municipality as 'celui établi dans la dernière liste publiée par l'Institut de la statistique du Québec' for that index as of 1 September of the fiscal year preceding the given fiscal year ('au 1er septembre de l'année financière qui précède l'année financière donnée', per the handoff's fuller extract of the same provision, whose opening words were verified verbatim against legisquebec 2026-08-07). This is a named institution and a named recurring publication ('la dernière liste publiée'), read on a dated schedule — the strongest evidence class short of a statutory formula.
dependencies.evidence_quote: celui établi dans la dernière liste publiée par l'Institut de la statistique du Québec

dependencies.basis: Auditor General of Ontario, 2023 follow-up on homelessness (report 1-07FU), describing the ministry's rebuilt HPP funding model: changes included 'replacing the outdated historical spending with measures of homelessness and supportive housing from Ontario Works and Ontario Disability Support Program caseload data, measures of supportive housing units using a survey administered to municipalities, and updated Statistics Canada data', and 'the updated funding model used four socioeconomic indicators (deep core housing need, low-income measure, Indigenous population, youth population), which accounted for half of the allocation calculation. All four indicators were updated using 2021 census data.' The final sentence names the release — the 2021 Census — which is what carries the edge past the agency-only test that removed five of six Statistics Canada rows from the OMPF Technical Guide. The primary statute (Housing Services Act, 2011 / O. Reg. 367/11) does not name the series; the model lives in program guidelines and transfer payment agreements, and the Auditor General is the published document that states it.

The handoff itself filed this with a null target: F-2.1, r. 11 s. 9 establishes standardized property value from the property assessment roll as reproduced in the municipal summary, and s. 8 takes the highest population of the current or prior three fiscal years as of 1 January (decree-based). Verified against legisquebec 2026-08-07: the regulation 'does not name Statistics Canada or ISQ' and 'identifies no specific statistical agency as the source' — inputs are municipal rolls and summaries, not published statistical releases. No named target, no edge. The qc-perequation node is kept as a deliberate isolated node because the regulation itself is the Quebec half of this slice's point and clearly qualifies as a consolidated-regulation node.

WRONG SOURCE, EDGE SURVIVES REMAPPED. The handoff attached the ISQ economic vitality index edge to qc-perequation while citing M-22.1, r. 1.2 as evidence — and its own _notes conceded 'the ISQ link is confined to the separate QST-growth apportionment regulation'. Verified 2026-08-07: M-22.1, r. 1.2 is the 'Règlement sur la répartition entre les municipalités du montant représentant la croissance d'une partie de la taxe de vente du Québec', a distinct transfer from the péréquation scheme under F-2.1, r. 11, and F-2.1, r. 11 nowhere names ISQ. The dependency is real but belongs to the QST-growth regulation, so a new node qc-partage-croissance-tvq was minted and the edge re-issued from it (see dependencies). Recorded so a later pass does not re-propose the péréquation version.

THE QUOTE IS REAL AND THE TARGET IS WRONG. Legal Aid Ontario's 2023-24 Annual Report states, verified verbatim 2026-08-07: 'LAO's current financial eligibility thresholds are aligned with the 2011 Low Income Measure', with the report explaining the LIM as a Statistics Canada threshold of households below 50% of average Canadian household income. But the Low Income Measure is an income-statistics product (historically SLID/T1FF, now the Canadian Income Survey family), not a Census of Population release — pointing this at statcan-census-population is the same substitution the corpus has previously rejected (the statcan-hfce case). It fails twice more: the alignment is to a frozen 2011 vintage rather than a recurring reading (the report's own point is that thresholds have NOT tracked the LIM since — sitting tens of percentage points below the 2020 LIM), and the operative thresholds are dollar amounts prescribed in the Legal Aid Services Rules, not computed from any release. If a statcan LIM/income-survey node is ever built, the right claim would be a historical methodology_depends_on at best. The on-legal-aid-ontario node is dropped with the edge: with no surviving dependency it would be an isolated node whose corpus fit is doubtful (the thresholds live inside the Legal Aid Services Rules, and the handoff's 'municipal-finance' domain tag did not fit it either).
